name: closing-key
scene:
TEN MINUTES AFTER CLOSING, in a narrow corner cafe built into an old brick storefront. The counter is dark walnut, worn pale in two arcs where elbows have rested for years. The espresso machine is a dulled chrome box with a chipped enamel badge. Three pendant bulbs hang at uneven heights on braided cords, each one pooling a small warm circle of light. The long window holds the rain: cold blue streaks run down the glass and break the sodium streetlight into thin lines across the floorboards.

Everything in the room is slightly out of place because a shift just ended. Two stoneware cups sit where they were put down, one with a dried ring inside. A folded cloth rests half off the counter's edge. A stack of saucers leans. A crumpled receipt has fallen under the stool. The chalkboard menu has been wiped down to a grey smear with three illegible marks left on it. The tip jar holds coins at different depths instead of a neat pile. A folded apron sits on the end of the counter.

The room's own light owns her: warm amber from the bulbs across her front, cold blue from the window along her back and along the edge of one ear.

She is dressed the way she dresses after the apron comes off: a black cropped cotton tee, its hem just at her ribs, tucked into black drawstring shorts; long slim digitigrade legs bare down to soft grey socks and scuffed canvas sneakers damp at the toes; a pair of over-ear headphones resting loose around her neck, one cup turned inward. One small glowing magenta-pink pendant hangs on a thin silver chain at her collarbone, the only glow on her body.
pose: Her body is turned three-quarters away from the window, weight settled on her right leg, left knee slightly bent, one hip dropped. Her right palm lies flat on the counter beside the folded cloth, fingers apart and relaxed, thumb clear of the edge so the whole hand is inside the frame. Her left hand is up at chest height pinching a single thin brass key between the tips of her thumb and forefinger, the key hanging straight down, the other three fingers curled loosely away from it so the palm stays open and visible, the sliver of light between thumb and index finger left clean. Her ears are relaxed, the left angled a little forward and the right leaning back. Her head is turned down and to her right; her eyes look down at the work on the counter, not into the lens, not at the viewer.
framing: Full-length distance shot, camera pulled back across the room on a 50mm lens at f/2.8, set at her chest height so the counter reads slightly from above. She stands at her full height and fills about 85 to 90 percent of the frame height, with clear empty space above both ear tips and visible floorboards below both shoes, everything inside the frame. Nothing cropped: both ears and both feet are in the picture with margin at the top and bottom edges, both hands fully inside the frame. Warm amber highlights against cool blue shadow, soft subsurface-scattered fur, shallow depth of field with the far wall falling off gently, fine film grain, no text, no watermark.
